people.gaius-letter.role: Man the elder loves, praised for helping traveling believers
people.gaius-letter.relations: The elder writes to him and calls him beloved. He asks Gaius to keep helping the brothers.
people.gaius-letter.meaning: Brothers come to the elder and tell how Gaius walks in truth. They say he cared for brothers who were strangers. They testified about his love before the assembly. The elder asks him to help them journey on in a way worthy of God.
people.diotrephes.role: Man in the assembly who loves to be first
people.diotrephes.relations: The elder wrote to the assembly, but Diotrephes did not accept what the elder said.
people.diotrephes.meaning: The elder says Diotrephes does not accept what the elder writes. He accuses the elder with wicked words. He does not receive the brothers himself. He forbids others to receive them and throws them out of the assembly. The elder says he will call attention to these deeds if he comes. We hear only the elder’s side.
people.demetrius-letter.role: Man with a good report from all
people.demetrius-letter.relations: The elder names him in a note to Gaius.
people.demetrius-letter.meaning: The elder says Demetrius has the testimony of all, and of the truth itself. The elder adds his own testimony. The letter says nothing more about him. It comes right after the warning about Diotrephes.
sources.web.summary: The full text of Third John is the main text for the close readings.
sources.web.limits: The text gives the elder no personal name. Gaius and Demetrius are not tied to people with the same names elsewhere. Authorship, dates, Greek forms, and the exact local setting were not checked independently. The letter gives no account from the opposing side. No such account was checked.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-49.summary: The lesson links joy to helping others walk in truth. It also warns against harmful conduct.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-49.limits: For Third John, the lesson covers verses 1–4 and 9–11. Linked Restoration texts and reference entries were not reviewed independently.
sources.usccb-3-john.summary: The introduction gives several possible reasons why Diotrephes refused to receive the brothers.
sources.usccb-3-john.limits: These are rival readings, not established reasons. Authorship, local offices, and the audience’s situation were not checked independently. A possible role for Demetrius as letter carrier was not checked either.
